why: R-B (owner, 2026-08-29; STATE §28): a bestiary placement asserts something MORE specific than a zone record does — an exact route band, exact depth tiers — so it must not be forced to inherit a region join that carries no geographic claim. Task 9's alphabetical-against-ascending-region-id pairing put `thornveil` on `c02/r30` for the zone-content ledger's own bookkeeping purposes only; ruling B keeps that join void here rather than loosen `content/schemas/bestiary-placement.schema.json`'s `zone` pattern (option A, rejected) or let the placement's own `routeBand` outrank the geography's `levelBand` (option C, rejected — the highest invented-content risk of the three). A placement file listed here is EXPECTED to fail G1's zone lookup; check_content.mjs downgrades that one failure to a WARN and skips G8 (there is no geography band to compare a voided join against). Every key here must correspond to a placement file whose zone genuinely does not resolve — the gate checks the bijection both ways, the same discipline content/spine/freeze-reasons.json already keeps for G-FROZEN, so this file cannot rot into covering a join that has since become real.

reasons.thornveil: 0 of 160 resolved zone ids can ever match content/schemas/bestiary-placement.schema.json's `zone` pattern (`^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` — no resolved zone id is a bare slug, every one is `cNN/rNN`), so no content edit joins this file to the drawn world at all. Its `routeBand` [15, 28] is canon.md's own bramble-forest band (A1 §4.2 zone 4), unrelated to c02/r30's fabric-assigned levelBand [8, 20], which is an artifact of Task 9's alphabetical pairing, not a design choice about Thornveil.
